the_one_metric: HPC/AI hosting revenue ramp under the CoreWeave contracts and any commitment for the ~500MW still unallocated to a customer; bitcoin mining economics are now background noise.
whats_priced_in: A sector-wide neocloud de-rating plus a Keefe downgrade the day before have already taken 24% out of the stock in 20 days, so the disappointment case is largely paid for.
bear_case: The last two prints fell 9.2% and 7.2%, the Keefe downgrade explicitly flagged risk to investor expectations, and with 86% realised vol any guidance wobble on contracted MW gets a double-digit down day.
key_drivers: run-up -23.75% over 20d and -8.84% on the session before the print: heavily de-risked
realised vol 86.1% annualised, median historical earnings move 6.54% - a fat-tailed print either way
Keefe downgrade 2026-07-27 on 'risk to investor expectations' (social, tier 3)
unallocated capacity is the binary: a new large-load contract is the upside tail
last two earnings reactions both negative (-9.22%, -7.22%)
what_would_change_my_mind: A contract announcement for the unallocated capacity alongside the print, or conversely any language walking back contracted HPC revenue timing.
reasoning: Anchors dominate here. A 24% twenty-day drawdown into a print, capped by a downgrade the prior session, cuts both ways: the bar is low but the tape says informed sellers. Corpus gives no consensus and no guidance, only sector colour and options flow that is two-sided (put sweeps then call sweeps). Direction is genuinely unresolved. The defensible answer is size: 86% vol and a 6.5% median historic reaction argue for roughly 9%, well above the proxy.

whats_priced_in: A clean community-bank quarter, with the stock already at its 52-week high after a 5.3% twenty-day advance.
bear_case: At the 52-week high with nothing left to beat on, a single credit surprise or an NIM guide-down produces a 3-4% day, far outside anything in the seven-print history.
key_drivers: seven prior reactions all inside +3.57%/-0.74%, median absolute 0.74%
realised vol only 20.3% annualised - the lowest-information print in the set

corpus is thin: no consensus, no guidance, no company-specific news in the window
no 8-K since 2026-05-01; recent Form 4s routine
what_would_change_my_mind: Any pre-print disclosure of a credit event, a securities restructuring charge, or an acquisition.
reasoning: A 126-branch community bank with 20% realised vol and seven consecutive sub-4% earnings reactions. The only corpus items are a CIO appointment and a Seeking Alpha round-up that does not discuss the company. There is no directional evidence, and manufacturing one would be fabrication. The confident claim is size: this print should move the stock under 2%, and I would take the under on any implied move above that. Direction is a coin flip and I am scoring it as such.

the_one_metric: Whether FY26 adjusted EPS guidance moves off $2.90-$3.00 and is formally raised to the upper half, after management said in April it was already 'trending toward the upper half'.
whats_priced_in: The upper-half FY26 EPS outcome and the buyback cadence are both already flagged, and the stock sits at its 52-week high, at the $64.23 consensus price target.
bear_case: Q1 beat by six cents on adjusted EPS with 140bp of EBITDA margin expansion, and a second straight beat plus a formal guidance raise on a name the sell side calls sleepy would snap the negative reaction pattern.
key_drivers: 5 of last 8 reactions negative, mean -2.01%; worst -8.19%
spot 64.09 at 52-week high, entire 20d gain (+5.64%) came in the final five sessions
spot sits at the $64.23 consensus target - no sell-side headroom
guidance already pre-announced as trending upper half of $2.90-$3.00: raise is expected, not a surprise

what_would_change_my_mind: A raise to the top of or above the $3.00 FY26 range together with core revenue growth accelerating past the 5.3% Q1 rate.
reasoning: The bar is documented and it is high. Management pre-signalled the upper half of FY26 guidance in April, so merely delivering it is neutral; the stock then rallied 5.6% in five sessions into the print to a 52-week high that equals the consensus target. FTV has a persistent negative post-print skew, five down in eight. That is a run-up-into-a-priced-story setup. Size, though, is well behaved: 24.5% vol and a 2.85% median argue about 3.2%, not a tail event.

the_one_metric: Q2 mitapivat net revenue and the AQVESME thalassemia prescription count versus the 242 written through 2026-03-31 - the first full launch quarter, with confirmation the sickle cell sNDA was actually filed in Q2 as guided.

bear_case: The Phase 2b tebapivat LR-MDS topline was guided for first-half 2026 and no 8-K reports it, so the print may have to disclose a slip or a soft result, and at 74% realised vol that is a double-digit down day.

tebapivat LR-MDS Phase 2b topline guided 1H26 and not yet disclosed - unresolved binary
prior print +13.10%; realised vol 73.7% - fat tails in both directions

what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence the Q2 sNDA filing slipped, or a tebapivat LR-MDS readout that misses on transfusion independence.
reasoning: First full commercial quarter for AQVESME against a trivially easy sequential comp, into a stock 23% off its high and drifting lower. Launch-quarter optics usually print well. Against that, the 1H26 tebapivat readout is undelivered and could arrive on the call in either form, which is why I keep direction small and size large. Seventy-four percent realised vol and a 13.1% reaction last quarter mean the 3.48% median proxy badly understates this print; 7% is my number.

bear_case: The 22% twenty-day slide is the market correctly front-running a large-load bookings deceleration, and with consensus at $3.31 EPS on $8.59bn revenue after two blowout prints the expectations bar embedded in estimates is still high even if the price is not.

what_would_change_my_mind: Total backlog flat or down sequentially, or full-year 2026 guidance merely reaffirmed rather than raised.
reasoning: The bar is sourced ($3.31 on $8.59bn) and the price into it has collapsed 22% in a month on sector sentiment rather than anything company-specific in the corpus. Q1 was a record with guidance raised across the board and record $48.5bn backlog. That asymmetry supports a lean up, but I hold it small: a drawdown that violent sometimes carries information I cannot see. Size is the higher-confidence claim - 35.5% vol plus +15.8% and +6.7% in the last two prints puts this near 7%, not the 3.85% median proxy.
